papers.summary: Spectral weight decay applies an additive nuclear-norm correction. In reported LLaMA experiments, it improves SVD-LLM compression over standard weight decay at matched validation loss.
papers.relevance: Direct match for spectral regularization, low-rank compressibility, and label-noise generalization.

evidence.quote: For the 500 500 M model and a 4 % 4\% distortion budget, it supports 1.89 × 1.89\times compression, compared with 1.14 × 1.14\times after standard weight decay.

papers.title: Spectral Weight Decay: Inducing Low-Rank Structure in Neural Network Weights

papers.summary: ORCA applies temporary soft orthogonality regularization early in LLM training. Reported LLaMA runs at 350M and 1.3B reduce final validation loss relative to Muon.
papers.relevance: Tests how training-time spectral shaping affects model quality across scales.

evidence.quote: Compared with Muon, ORCA reduces the final loss by 0.0194 0.0194 at 350M and 0.0244 0.0244 at 1.3B, with consistent gains at both scales.

papers.title: ORCA: The Annealed Spectral Conditioning Optimizer for Faster, Better LLM Training

papers.summary: Analyzes how optimizer geometry and depth govern the emergence, saturation, and decay of singular modes in balanced, aligned deep matrix factorization.
papers.relevance: Provides a theoretical framework for optimizer-dependent spectral bias, subject to its balance and alignment assumptions.

evidence.quote: Although the phase laws rely on balance and alignment assumptions, they identify concrete mechanisms to understand optimizer behavior.

papers.title: Optimizer Geometry Sets the Pace: Spectral Learning Dynamics in Matrix Factorization

papers.summary: Selectively orthogonalizes momentum singular subspaces in NanoGPT experiments. Amplifying small singular directions nearly matches full Muon, while targeting only the largest directions eventually underperforms.
papers.relevance: Directly probes Muon, singular-value spectra, effective rank, and language-model optimization.

evidence.quote: Orthogonalizing everything except the few largest singular values of each matrix gets within 0.03 of Muon while orthogonalizing only about 13% of the momentum matrix’s magnitude

papers.title: Spectrally Targeted Muon

papers.summary: Derives LoRA rank bounds from finite-rank maps induced by frozen features, without NTK linearization. Its stationary-point result requires a generic perturbation and does not rule out spurious local minima.
papers.relevance: Addresses the geometry and optimization landscape of low-rank adaptation.

evidence.quote: This is a first-order exclusion theorem, not a no-spurious-local-minima theorem; Proposition 4.9 gives an explicit limitation.

papers.title: How Finite-Rank Bottlenecks Shape the Low-Rank Adaptation Landscape

papers.summary: Proposes a Riemannian preconditioner for LoRA and tests it on GPT-2 generation and LLaMA2-7B commonsense fine-tuning with fixed ranks and tuned learning rates.
papers.relevance: Connects LoRA parameterization geometry to practical language-model fine-tuning.

evidence.quote: We also fixed the rank to r = 32 r=32 , the scaling factor of B ​ A ⊤ BA^{\top} to 64 64 , the batch size to 16 16 , the weight decay to zero, the dropout to 0.05 0.05 , and the train epoch to 3 3 with a linear learning-rate schedule.

papers.title: A Riemannian Geometry for Low-rank Adaptation

papers.summary: Combines Monarch-structured weights with Muon. Its complete quality runs are separate from larger-scale systems measurements, where the reported 6.89B reference shows lower peak memory and full-step time than dense Muon.
papers.relevance: Addresses pretraining quality, memory, and runtime tradeoffs as model width grows.

evidence.quote: At 6.89B, Monarch–Muon reduces the full-step time by 45% and peak memory by 23% relative to dense Muon.

Systems benchmarks cover dense reference sizes up to 6.89B on an H100. These benchmarks measure the cost of the training operations at larger widths, while the complete pretraining runs test learning quality.

papers.title: Monarch-Muon: Structure-Aware Muon for Fast and Memory-Efficient Pretraining

papers.summary: PMRC keeps momentum in a low-dimensional subspace while adding an orthogonal residual gradient to the update. Reported C4 pretraining compares it with AdamW, Muon, GaLore, GoLore, Fira, and GUM.
papers.relevance: Direct match for memory-efficient LLM pretraining and low-rank optimizer-state methods.

evidence.quote: PMRC consistently achieves the lowest training and validation losses among memory-efficient methods.

papers.title: Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon

papers.summary: CORE combines passage retrieval, snippet selection, source expansion, and deduplication in a training-free deep-research harness. Its closed-search comparisons report higher answer accuracy and evidence recall than two evaluated harnesses.
papers.relevance: Directly informs retrieval and context management for a handwritten research-digest agent.

evidence.quote: Across three agent models and three benchmarks, CORE achieves higher answer accuracy and evidence recall than Tongyi DeepResearch and OpenResearcher in every model–benchmark comparison, while returning substantially fewer tokens per search than Tongyi DeepResearch.

papers.title: CORE: Coarse-to-Fine Search with Context Management for Deep Research

papers.summary: Idea2Prior presents an auditable idea-to-paper retrieval and ranking workflow with bounded PDF evidence. Its historical Hit@5 advantage is concentrated in EASY and MEDIUM queries, not HARD.
papers.relevance: Directly applicable to paper discovery, evidence tracking, and relevance ranking in the digest agent.

evidence.quote: The small, overlapping target set and historical protocol do not support a broad or statistically established superiority claim.
Idea2Prior leads both baselines by 20 percentage points on EASY and MEDIUM, but trails ChatGPT by 10 points on HARD.

papers.title: Idea2Prior: Auditable Paper Retrieval and Ranking from Research Ideas
